title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY: Health Cover & Eligibility
content: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides a health cover of Rs 5 Lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation care across empanelled public and private hospitals in India. There is no cap on family size or age. Eligibility is based on SECC 2011 deprivation criteria (rural and urban) or senior citizens aged 70+ (under expanded 2024-2026 guidelines). No enrollment fee is required; eligible beneficiaries can make their Ayushman Golden Card via pmjay.gov.in, the Ayushman App, or at any empanelled hospital (Ayushman Mitra desk).

title: Ayushman Bharat: Hospital Cashless Treatment & Grievance Redressal
content: All treatments under PM-JAY are completely cashless and paperless for eligible cardholders. The hospital cannot charge any cash for medicines, diagnostics, or surgery covered in package rates. In case of illegal demand of money or refusal of treatment by an empanelled hospital: 1) Contact the hospital's on-site Ayushman Mitra or Nodal Officer. 2) Call National Toll-Free Helpline 14555 or 1800-111-565. 3) File online grievance on Central Grievance Redressal Management System (CGRMS) at cgrms.pmjay.gov.in.
source_url_or_file: NHA Operational Guidelines on Beneficiary Rights

title: EPFO: Online PF Advance & Withdrawal Rules (Form 31, 19, 10C)
content: EPFO members can withdraw Provident Fund (PF) balance online through the Unified Member Portal (epfindia.gov.in) using UAN and password. Types of Claims: 1) Form 31 (PF Advance/Partial Withdrawal): Allowed for illness (immediate, no minimum service required), marriage/education (7 years service), house purchase/construction (5 years service). 2) Form 19 (Final PF Settlement): Allowed only after 2 months of leaving employment (or immediate on retirement). 3) Form 10C (Pension Withdrawal Benefit): If total service is less than 9.5 years. Prerequisites: Aadhaar linked with UAN, Bank account with IFSC seeded and approved by employer, active mobile for OTP.

title: EPFO: Claim Rejection Reasons & EPFiGMS Grievance Portal
content: Common reasons for EPFO claim rejection: 1) Name/Father's name/DOB mismatch between Aadhaar and Member Profile (fix via Joint Declaration form online). 2) Bank account number or IFSC mismatch or unreadable cancelled cheque upload. 3) Date of Exit not marked by previous employer (can now be marked by employee online after 2 months of leaving). To file a grievance for delayed PF claim or employer non-cooperation: Register complaint on EPFiGMS (epfigms.gov.in). Resolution SLA is 15-20 days.

title: Cyber Financial Fraud: Golden Hours Helpline 1930 & Reporting
content: If money is fraudulently debited from your bank account, UPI (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm), or credit card: Step 1: Immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 (operated by I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs). Reporting within the 'Golden Hour' (first 2-3 hours) allows police and banks to freeze the money in transit before the scammer withdraws it. Step 2: Register formal cyber complaint with transaction IDs, screenshots, and bank SMS on cybercrime.gov.in. Step 3: Inform your bank within 3 days (under RBI Zero Liability guidelines) to secure zero liability protection.
source_url_or_file: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C - cybercrime.gov.in)

title: One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) & NFSA Food Grain Entitlements
content: Under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) and One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) scheme, eligible beneficiaries (Antyodaya Anna Yojana - AAY and Priority Household - PHH) can collect their entitled free food grains from ANY Fair Price Shop (ration shop) across India using biometric Aadhaar authentication. AAY households receive 35 kg per family per month, and PHH beneficiaries receive 5 kg per person per month. Migrant workers do not need to cancel their home state ration card to get ration in other cities. Toll-Free PDS Helpline: 1967 or state food helpline.

title: Driving Licence & Learner Licence (Sarathi Parivahan) Online Process
content: Under MoRTH contactless citizen services on sarathi.parivahan.gov.in: 1) Learner Licence (LL): Can be applied and tested online from home using Aadhaar authentication (no RTO visit required in most states). Valid for 6 months. 2) Permanent Driving Licence (DL): Can be applied after 30 days of LL issuance and requires booking a physical driving skill test slot at RTO. 3) Address change, renewal, duplicate DL, and NOC can be done completely online with Aadhaar OTP.

title: Right to Information (RTI) Act 2005: Filing Online Application
content: Under the Right to Information Act 2005, every Indian citizen has the right to request information from Public Authorities (Central & State govt departments, PSUs, public universities). Application Fee: Rs 10 (free for BPL cardholders). Central Govt RTIs can be filed online at rtionline.gov.in. Time limit for response: 30 days (48 hours if it concerns life or liberty). If no reply is received or information is denied, a First Appeal can be filed within 30 days with the First Appellate Authority (FAA) of that department.
source_url_or_file: Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT / rtionline.gov.in)

title: Voter ID (EPIC): New Voter Registration & Online Correction Forms
content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) provides citizen services on voters.eci.gov.in and Voter Helpline App (Helpline: 1950): 1) Form 6: Application for New Voter Registration (Indian citizens turning 18+). 2) Form 8: Correction of entries in existing electoral roll (Name, Photo, Address change, Shifting of residence, Mobile number linking). 3) Download e-EPIC: Digital PDF voter card with QR code can be downloaded by linking mobile number with EPIC. Processing timeline is typically 15-30 days by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) / Booth Level Officer (BLO).

title: UIDAI Aadhaar: Demographic Update, Address Change & Biometrics
content: Under UIDAI regulations (uidai.gov.in / Toll-Free 1947): 1) Address Update: Can be done completely online via myAadhaar portal (myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in) with valid Proof of Address (Electricity bill, Rent agreement, Bank statement) or Head of Family (HoF) consent. Fee: Rs 50. 2) Mobile Number & Email Linkage: Requires biometric verification at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra / Post Office (cannot be done online without OTP). Fee: Rs 50. 3) Mandatory Biometric Update for Children: Free at age 5 and age 15. 4) Document Update: Free periodically on myAadhaar to keep demographic proof active.

title: PM Jan Aushadhi Scheme (PMBJP): Affordable Generic Medicines
content: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) provides high-quality generic medicines, surgical items, and sanitary pads at 50% to 90% cheaper prices compared to branded market medicines. All medicines sold at Jan Aushadhi Kendras are tested at NABL-accredited laboratories for WHO-GMP quality compliance. To find nearby kendras and check medicine salt price comparisons, citizens can use the 'Jan Aushadhi Sugam' mobile app or visit janaushadhi.gov.in (National Helpline: 1800-180-8080).
source_url_or_file: Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI - janaushadhi.gov.in)

title: Constitution of India: Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12-35)
content: The Constitution of India guarantees Fundamental Rights to every citizen: 1) Article 14: Equality before law and equal protection of laws. 2) Article 15: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth in public places/services. 3) Article 19: Six basic freedoms including Freedom of Speech and Expression, peaceful assembly, movement, and trade/occupation. 4) Article 21: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty (Supreme Court has expanded this to include Right to Privacy, Health, Clean Environment, Shelter, and Dignified Livelihood). 5) Article 21A: Right to Free and Compulsory Education for all children aged 6 to 14 years.
source_url_or_file: Constitution of India (Ministry of Law & Justice)

title: Article 39A & Free Legal Aid (NALSA / Tele-Law Helpline 15100)
content: Under Article 39A of the Constitution of India and the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, the State is mandated to provide free and competent legal aid to marginalized citizens to ensure justice is not denied due to economic or other disabilities. Eligible for 100% Free Legal Aid: Women, children, SC/ST members, industrial workers, persons with disabilities, victims of trafficking/disaster, and persons in police or judicial custody. Citizens can access free government advocates through District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA), Taluk Legal Services Committees, or by dialing Tele-Law National Toll-Free Helpline 15100 / nalsa.gov.in.

title: Constitutional Remedies & Writs (Article 32 & Article 226)
content: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar termed Article 32 as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'. Citizens whose Fundamental Rights are violated can directly petition the Supreme Court under Article 32 or High Courts under Article 226. Types of Constitutional Writs: 1) Habeas Corpus ('To have the body'): Orders authorities to produce an illegally detained person before the court. 2) Mandamus ('We command'): Directs a public official or government department to perform their mandatory statutory duty. 3) Prohibition: Stops a lower court/tribunal from exceeding jurisdiction. 4) Certiorari: Quashes an illegal order passed by a lower authority. 5) Quo Warranto: Questions the legal authority of a person holding a public office.
source_url_or_file: Supreme Court of India Constitutional Jurisprudence

title: Police Arrest Safeguards & Citizen Rights (Article 22 & D.K. Basu Rules)
content: Under Article 22 of the Constitution, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Supreme Court's landmark D.K. Basu judgment: 1) Right to Know Grounds of Arrest: Police must inform the arrested person of the exact reason and charges immediately. 2) Memo of Arrest: Must be prepared at the spot with signature of at least one witness/family member. 3) Right to Inform Family: Police must inform one relative/friend within 8-12 hours of arrest. 4) 24-Hour Magistrate Rule: Arrested person MUST be produced before the nearest Judicial Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding travel time); detention beyond 24 hours without magistrate order is unconstitutional. 5) Medical Examination: Arrested person has the right to be medically examined every 48 hours in custody. 6) Female Arrest: Women cannot be arrested before sunrise or after sunset without special permission from a Judicial Magistrate, and must be handled by female police officers.
source_url_or_file: Supreme Court of India (D.K. Basu vs State of West Bengal / Article 22)
